newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN reports wave of ethnic killings in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN reports wave of ethnic killings in Rwanda.

text.p: The United Nations voiced concern on Tuesday at 344 ethnically-motivated killings in Rwanda and with the safety of local journalists after the murder of two.

The U.N. human rights office said state agents including Rwandan troops were blamed for 162 of the reported killings over a six-week period until mid-May, including 152 people slain by soldiers in the northwestern border region of Ruhengeri alone.
It said Rwandan troops killed at least 137 civilians in a single operation in one day in Ruhengeri, a predominantly Hutu area where the Tutsi-dominated army faces an uphill battle.

It had no word on abuses committed against Hutu refugees, more than 800,000 of whom have returned to Rwanda from Zaire to where they had fled in fear of reprisal for the 1994 genocide of more than half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
Most refugees returned to border regions which have become no-go areas for Western relief workers because of a guerrilla war between the army and rebels of Rwanda's Hutu majority.
U.N. refugee agency spokesman Pamela O'Toole, said: "We cannot monitor returning refugees in most areas for lack of security. We can't do all we'd like on protection."
The U.N. human rights report said Hutu rebels were blamed for 51 killings in the period between March 1 and mid-May.

The editor of Umuravumba magazine and a writer for Intego journal were killed in the capital Kigali at the end of April. "The U.N. Human Rights Office in Rwanda is concerned about the security of other journalists," the U.N. report added.
